name: Apoxy

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: CLRK Free
plans.note: Hosted CLRK not live: button 'Coming soon'. 1 Connected Worker, default-deny egress, 7-day logs; no dedicated egress IP.

plans.name: CLRK Standard
plans.note: Coming soon. Unlimited Connected Workers; 1 TB bandwidth then $0.05/GB; 10 GB logs then $0.25/GB; dedicated egress IP +$20/mo. No per-vCPU/RAM rate published.

plans.name: CLRK Enterprise
plans.note: Hosted agents in your VPC; talk to a founder.

caveats: Edge JS/TS/Wasm workers bundled with routing: Free 100GB traffic, Standard $80/mo including 1TB then $0.05/GB; TCP/UDP +$20/gateway. CLRK is gVisor-isolated agent runtime: free 1 connected worker; paid Standard $80 and Enterprise displayed coming-soon. BYOC Premium annual from $2k/mo, per-vCPU price unpublished. Do not treat edge traffic tariff as free 4/8 VM.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
Logs/traces: Free 1 GB (7-day), Standard 10 GB (30-day) then $0.25/GB; TCP/UDP gateways +$20/gateway/month on Standard; Free cannot exceed the included bucket (hard cap default, no overage).

Apoxy bandwidth is gateway/proxy traffic (max of client ingress/egress, origin traffic free), not sandbox VM egress: Free includes 100 GB/month (hard cap, no overage); Standard ($80/mo) includes 1 TB then $0.05/GB, volume tiered.

Nested virtualization set to no: every sandbox runs under gVisor, which gives the workload its own user-space kernel and no /dev/kvm device (no KVM-based emulators or VMs inside). Docker inside is a separate question.

fleet.tiers: Free and paid Platform/CLRK offerings; Enterprise/BYOC terms negotiated.
fleet.notes: Pricing separates network Platform from agent runtime. Reviewed public pricing does not establish aggregate new-account sandbox/vCPU/GPU quotas or a quota-review timeline. Platform bandwidth and annual-contract scale claims are not sandbox concurrency.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: CLRK sandboxes have no durable cross-worker persistent storage by default. Each invocation starts from a fresh rootfs; `/tmp` and any image-baked filesystem state reset on every run.
snapshot_auto.note: Ephemeral per-invocation gVisor sandboxes; state must live outside (or in the small TaskAgent.spec.state mount).

harness_api.quote: A `TaskAgent` named `jq-bot` that accepts a JSON body, runs the `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` CLI inside a fresh sandbox per request, and returns the model's structured output.
harness_api.note: CLRK is a generic agent runtime: a TaskAgent is YOUR container image invoked per HTTP request (JSON body -> CloudEvents on stdin, stdout -> response), plus cron schedules and DaemonAgents. Claude Code is only an example you package yourself; no first-party API to prompt a harness, send follow-ups, or list/resume conversations ('The TaskAgent response model is request/response'; conversation state is a user pattern with external Postgres). Borderline: the invocation/streaming contract is first-party but harness-agnostic.

egress_allowlist.quote: CLRK's `EgressGateway` defaults to `deny-all` - egress is closed unless you open it. ... `EgressL4Route` declares allowed L4 destinations: `destinationCIDRs`, `destinationHostnames`, `ports`, `protocol` (TCP or UDP).
egress_allowlist.note: Enforced at the worker dialer/Envoy egress gateway outside the gVisor sandbox. Hostname matching via DNS snooping/SNI (docs warn DoH/DoT or lying SNI weaken hostname rules; pair with CIDRs). Optional per-agent scoping via sourceAgents label selector; EgressDenyPolicy for default-allow gateways.

egress_http_rules.quote: | `endpoints` | string[] | Endpoints restricts to API paths. |
egress_http_rules.note: L7 rules on the TLS-terminating (MITM) egress gateway: AIProviderRoute matches provider + endpoint paths + models (provider 'custom' = 'endpoint-only matching'), with token budgets, RateLimitPolicy, header rewrites (credential injection) and EgressDenyPolicy returning an HTTP deny response (default 403). No generic HTTP method/header match rules documented; mainly aimed at LLM/MCP traffic.

ingress_rules.quote: CLRK does not authenticate the requests that reach its ingress. There is no built-in OIDC validator, no JWT verifier, no API-key middleware.
ingress_rules.note: Sandboxes are not directly addressable; only TaskAgents get a per-agent Envoy ingress (DaemonAgents have none), a cluster-internal Service in the operator's own Kubernetes. Access control is left to your own auth proxy / K8s networking. (Apoxy's separate edge Gateway product has its own routing, not assessed here.)

secret_proxy.quote: ParentRefs attaches this policy to AIProviderRoute, MCPRoute, or EgressGateway listeners. ... EgressGateway: catch-all for any traffic on the gateway that no narrower policy claimed.
secret_proxy.note: Egress proxy terminates TLS (per-gateway CA trusted in the sandbox) and injects a K8s Secret as Header, QueryParam or ProviderAuth (AWS SigV4 / GCP service account); agent sees placeholder 'clrk-injected-by-proxy' ('The agent process never holds them'). Agent-set headers are overwritten. HTTP(S) only; raw TCP routes (e.g. Postgres) are allowlisted but no credential injection for non-HTTP protocols documented. MCPRoute injection 'no-op until MCPRoute consumption ships'.
